Handheld operator LOCOMOTION -- what the operator is physically doing, as distinct from Operator Style which is what rig they are holding. 0 Legacy (the Motion Profile axis stays in charge; stock behaviour), 1 Creep, 2 Walk, 3 Run, 4 Drive, 5 Float, 6 Unsteady, 100 Auto. Selecting any mode other than Legacy REPLACES the Motion Profile axis rather than stacking with it. Modes never overwrite your authored settings.

[ActorMover] Ghost-walk ground speed in m/s. Client-side only: the sim never sees the movement; the walk animation clock is scaled to match so foot plants never slide.

[ActorMover] Ground speed the walk animation was authored for (cadence reference). Tune until feet lock to the ground at your working speed.

[ActorMover] Actor pathing: maximum facing turn rate in degrees/second while walking a path. Sharp corners ease toward the new heading at this rate instead of snapping; straightaways are unaffected. Lower = lazier turns, higher = snappier.

[ActorMover] Per-node path camera master switch (session tool). When on, the cameras a director authored on Subject A's path drive the render camera as that actor walks, so a walk plays as one actor+camera take. Off (default) is a byte-identical no-op: the new camera source never engages and existing pathing is unchanged. The camera releases back to the normal agent camera the moment the walk stops, finishes, is cut, or the actor derezzes / leaves the region.
[ActorMover] On: Walk/Stop drive every roster actor with the shared parameters. Off: Walk/Stop apply only to the actor selected in the roster list, so actors can run different speeds/headings.

[ActorMover] Show path: draw the in-world path preview for each roster/cast actor. With a walkable path (2+ nodes) this is the thick outlined spline with direction chevrons and numbered node markers (start green, end red, dwell nodes ringed); with no path it is the thick straight heading arrow along the planned travel bearing (current facing + heading trim) for the configured distance. Client-side overlay only; rendered while the Actor Mover or Director floater is open.

[GhostDeferred] Log per-frame Ghost Studio deferred-proxy P0/P1 queue and render-invariant counters (proxies built/culled/submitted, batch accept/reject, invariant violations). Diagnostics only; off by default.

[GhostDeferred] One-shot G-buffer contamination test control (0 = idle, 1 = arm, 2 = cancel). Captures the deferred G-buffer with the ghost deferred submission OFF vs ON and reports PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE. Diagnostics only.
[GhostDeferred] Pixel padding added around each ghost proxy's screen-space bounds when masking it out of the G-buffer contamination diff (conservative, avoids rasterization edge false-positives).
Ghost Studio body-turn speed in degrees per second. How fast a clone rotates toward its turn target. Body turn is rate-limited so it reads as a deliberate move; look-at still snaps.
Ghost Studio body-turn ease band, in radians. Within this much of the target the clone decelerates into position instead of stopping dead. Larger = a longer, softer settle.
Draw an in-world preview of the active crowd-placement draft -- numbered slot markers, guides, and an enclosing perimeter -- before you commit it. Costs nothing when no placement draft is active.

[GhostDeferred] EXPERIMENTAL: submit Ghost Studio CLONE-style clones into the deferred G-buffer so they receive real scene lighting (rigged opaque+masked only for now) instead of the fullbright post-tonemap overlay. Off by default; wrap the submission in the render-state invariant check. Toggling off returns to stock rendering.
[GhostStudio] EXPERIMENTAL: entity clones retain valid source-resolved BoM/material texture bindings across refresh and rebuild. Off by default pending material/pass/topology acceptance.
[GhostStudio] EXPERIMENTAL: exclude temporary world attachments in the shared source enumerator. Off preserves current Overlay and Entity behavior. HUD attachments are always excluded.

[ActorMover] Pose/blocking ghosts: draw copies of the actor at every node of its walkable path so blocking reads without pressing ACTION. The default renderer is the true 3D model ghost (PathGhostUseModel), whose LOOK is picked by PathGhostStyle (ghost / clone / hologram / wireframe / x-ray); the impostor billboard (PathGhostUseImpostor) and the stick figure are fallbacks, tinted to the actor. Shows only while the path preview (ActorMoverShowHeading) is on and the Actor Mover / Director floater is open. Off by default; adds no per-frame cost when off.

[BDMerge G3.2] Godray raymarch sample count (16-128; donor default 32). Higher = smoother shafts, more GPU.
[BDMerge G3.2] Godray brightness multiplier (0.01-30; donor default 1.0).
[BDMerge G3.2] Godray distance falloff multiplier (donor default 1.0). Higher fades shafts out closer to the camera.

[BDMerge G3.3] Enable per-projector volumetric light cones (visible spotlight shafts) from shadow-casting projectors. Independent of RenderVolumetricLighting (the sun godrays), but like it requires shadows (RenderShadowDetail > 0) - the shaft is self-shadowed by each projector's own shadow map. NET-NEW local-light effect (not a Black Dragon port).

[BDMerge G3.3] Projector shaft raymarch sample count (8-64; default 16). This is a BOUNDED local march - every sample lands inside the cone's range, so far fewer samples are needed than the sun godrays' 32. Cost scales with this x the number of shadow-casting projectors.
[BDMerge G3.3] Projector shaft brightness multiplier (0.01-30; default 1.0). Primary in-world tuning lever for shaft intensity.

[BDMerge G3.3] Henyey-Greenstein scattering anisotropy g (0.0-0.95; default 0.72). Forward-scatter: higher = brighter glow when the camera looks toward the projector, dimmer from the side. 0 = isotropic.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Projector shaft march-start dither. 0 = off (banding at low sample counts), 1 = static blue-noise (interleaved gradient; stable per screen-pixel so it never shimmers under camera motion - recommended for recording), 2 = animated blue-noise (adds a subtle per-frame rotation that averages residual banding on still shots but can shimmer slightly in motion). Default 1.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Projector shaft cone-edge feather (0.0-0.5; default 0.15). Softens the angular beam boundary so the cone edge is not a hard line; the value is the fraction of the cookie half-width over which the shaft fades out. 0 = hard edge.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Projector shaft occlusion sub-taps per march step (1-4; default 1). 1 = one shadow tap per step (cheap). Higher values sub-sample the shadow map between march steps so thin occluders (bars, foliage) resolve into crisp god-ray bands through the beam. Cost scales with this x resolution x projector count.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Restrict each projector shaft's fullscreen raymarch to the screen rectangle its sphere of influence actually covers (glScissor). Skips the majority of off-cone fragment work at no visual cost. Default on; disable only to diagnose clipping.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Adaptively scale the raymarch sample count per cone by its on-screen size: distant/small cones use fewer samples (down to the floor below), a cone filling the view uses the full Resolution. Default on. Disable to force every cone to the full Resolution.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] March the projector volumetric cones into a half-resolution buffer and depth-aware bilateral-upsample the result onto the scene. Quarters the marched fragment work - the biggest FPS lever with multiple flagged projectors - at a small softening of very thin shaft detail. Default on; turn off for the fullscreen (sharpest) path.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Floor for the adaptive sample count (4-32; default 6). A cone never marches with fewer than this many samples regardless of how small it is on screen. Ignored when Adaptive is off.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 1] Linear-HDR headroom clamp per cone (1.0-64.0; default 8.0). Because the shaft now composites in linear HDR before the tonemapper, this is a generous ceiling that guards against NaN/inf and lone fireflies while still letting the tonemapper roll off bright cores - not the tight display-space clamp the old post-tonemap placement used.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch A - E1] Bound each projector shaft's raymarch by the light's actual frustum (4 side planes + near) instead of only its sphere of influence. For narrow cones this tightens the marched interval several-fold, so the same sample budget gives a cleaner shaft (or the budget can be lowered for free). Look-neutral: the clipped interval is a strict superset of the lit region and falls back to the sphere bounds if degenerate. Default on.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch A - E2] Take a single interleaved-gradient-jittered self-shadow tap per march step instead of ShadowSamples sub-taps (up to 4x fewer shadow-map fetches, the loop's most expensive op). The per-pixel dither already offsets the tap along the step so it decorrelates like the sub-taps and the dither/temporal path averages it. When on, ShadowSamples>1 is ignored. Default off (A/B baseline); keep off with Temporal off for fully deterministic sub-taps.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 2] Art-direction tint for flagged projector shafts (linear RGB). Blended toward by TintStrength so the shaft can carry a color that differs from the light's own color. Applies globally to every session-flagged shaft; default 1,1,1 (with TintStrength 0) is a no-op.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 2] How strongly the shaft color is pulled toward Tint, away from the light's own color (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = pure light color, 1.0 = pure Tint). Applies to all session-flagged shafts.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Global participating-medium density / haziness master for all flagged projector shafts (0.0-4.0; default 1.0). One multiplier scaling the whole shaft density for per-shot atmosphere: <1 thins the beam, >1 makes the air hazier. 1.0 = the shipped look (no-op).

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Animated 3D noise medium strength (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = OFF). Modulates shaft density with a slow, low-frequency world-anchored fbm so the beam has drifting dust motes / gentle turbulence instead of a flat cone. TASTEFUL LEVER: keep it low - a subtle cinematic value is ~0.2-0.35; high values look grainy and are an explicit non-goal. Default OFF (flat cone, the shipped look).

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Spatial scale of the animated noise medium in cycles per metre (0.01-2.0; default 0.15). Lower = larger, softer, more cinematic dust clouds; higher = finer (grainier) detail. Only active when NoiseStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Scroll speed of the animated noise medium in metres per second (0.0-2.0; default 0.15). Slow drift reads as gently settling dust; fast scroll looks artificial. Only active when NoiseStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Height-based fog density strength (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = OFF). Blends the shaft density toward an altitude-dependent falloff (denser near ground, thinner up high) so shafts have atmospheric depth and sit in the air. 0 = uniform density (the shipped look).

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Height fog density multiplier at/below the ground reference altitude (0.0-4.0; default 1.0). The shaft is densest here and thins with altitude per FogFalloff. Only active when FogStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Height fog e-fold falloff distance in metres (0.5-256.0; default 24.0). Over this many metres of altitude above the ground reference the density falls to ~37% of the ground value. Larger = the fog reaches higher. Only active when FogStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Ground reference altitude for height fog, in region-Z metres (default 0.0). Density equals FogGroundDensity at and below this height and thins above it. Set to the floor height of your set for shafts that pool at ground level. Only active when FogStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Phase 3] Controlled feed of the shaft into the HDR bloom pyramid for a soft glow halo around bright cores (0.0-2.0; default 0.0 = OFF). A separate, scaled, tent-blurred additive of the half-res shaft into the bloom buffer AFTER the pyramid is built from the clean scene - so it never reintroduces uncontrolled bloom leakage; the scene bloom itself is unchanged. Requires HalfRes on (uses the half-res shaft) and the HDR path. Keep modest (~0.15-0.4).

[BDMerge G3.3 item C4] Anamorphic stretch of the projector-volumetric bloom-feed halo (1.0-4.0; default 1.0 = OFF/exact isotropic tent). Scales the X tap spacing of the bloom-feed tent blur (Y unchanged) so the fed halo streaks horizontally - the classic anamorphic streak on beam cores AND the rim glow (they ride the same feed). Only has an effect when BDMergeProjectorVolumetricsBloomFeed > 0; try BloomFeed ~0.3 with this at 2.0-3.0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch 1] Enable across-frame temporal reprojection accumulation for the projector shafts. Blends each frame's shaft with a reprojected, neighborhood-clamped, disocclusion/camera-cut-rejected copy of the previous frame so the shaft is smoother and stays stable with fewer march samples. Neighborhood clamp bounds the result to the current frame so it cannot ghost or smear - a static scene converges to the current look, just denoised. Requires Half-res on (the accumulation lives in the half-res history targets). Default on.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch 1] Temporal accumulation history weight / EMA blend (0.0-0.98; default 0.75). Higher = more history retained = smoother and more stable but slower to react to change; lower = more responsive but noisier. Only active when Temporal is on.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch B] Contrast-aware temporal anti-ghost strength (0.0-8.0; default 3.5). Reduces the temporal history weight in proportion to how much the beam is changing frame-to-frame at each pixel, so a steady shaft still denoises but moving/high-contrast features snap to the current frame instead of leaving a trail. Higher = more aggressive ghost suppression (and slightly noisier on motion); 0 = off (ghosting bounded only by the neighborhood clamp). Only active when Temporal is on.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch B] Reproject the BEAM, not the wall behind it (default on). The projector shaft is airborne, so under camera motion the mid-air scatter and the opaque surface behind it move differently. The march writes an overlap-safe luminance-premultiplied first distance moment into the half-res target's alpha; the temporal pass recovers the mean beam distance and reprojects/disocclusion-tests with that point. Only active when Temporal is on (which requires Half-res). Off retains the legacy surface-based temporal path.

[BDMerge G3.3 Batch 1] Gobo-colored occluder shadow strength (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = classic hard black occluder shadow). When above 0, occluded march samples still carry a dimmed, gobo-shaped colored contribution so occluders tint/dim the beam like stained glass (colored god-ray banding shaped by the projector's cookie) instead of punching pure-black holes. Keep subtle (~0.1-0.3). True colored-occluder shadows (the occluder's own albedo tinting the beam) would need a colored spot shadow map - documented as a follow-up.

[BDMerge G3.3 Rim] Physical DIRECTIONAL rim / wrap glow strength around objects the projector actually lights (0.0-4.0; default 0.0 = OFF). At the opaque surface capping the shaft march, the projector's real incident light (gobo cookie x distance attenuation x this projector's own shadow map) is placed only where the light RAKES the form - grazing silhouette (real G-buffer normal, N.V) AND facing the projector (N.L wrap, see RimWrap). So only edges the light physically wraps around glow, carrying the light's color; a frontal/camera-position light produces no rim (correct). Brightness is internally scaled for finer slider control - the sweet spot is around ~0.75 (roughly 0.5-1.5 usable), not tiny fractions. SOFT HALO: the rim is added into the HDR shaft, so turning on BDMergeProjectorVolumetricsHalfRes + a small BDMergeProjectorVolumetricsBloomFeed (~0.2-0.4) blooms it into a soft glow hugging the lit silhouette.

[BDMerge G3.3 Rim] Rim grazing (Fresnel) exponent (0.5-8.0; default 2.0). How tightly the glow clings to the silhouette: higher = a thin bright edge only at the extreme grazing angle; lower = a broader band reaching onto the form. Works together with RimWrap (which sets how far past the light terminator it reaches). Only active when RimStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Rim] Rim directional wrap (0.0-1.0; default 0.35). Sets how far past the light/shadow terminator the rim reaches around the form. 0 = a crisp rim only on the strictly light-facing silhouette (pure back-light); higher softens the terminator and wraps the glow further onto the body as interior fill. This is the term that makes the rim directional instead of a uniform outline. Only active when RimStrength > 0.

[BDMerge G3.3 Rim] Incident-light floor for the rim (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = no gate). Surfaces receiving projector light dimmer than this do not glow, so faint ambient spill can't grey the rim - raise to keep the rim only on brightly, directly lit surfaces (soft smoothstep gate). Only active when RimStrength > 0.

[BDMerge F4] Rim SKIN SOFTNESS for avatar rims (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = exact current look). Smoothstep-shapes the rim's grazing falloff so an avatar edge reads as a soft glow bleeding onto skin instead of a hard, cutout-like outline. 0 = identity (unchanged); raise toward 1 to progressively soften the transition. Only active when RimStrength > 0. Per-projector capturable (Shaft: capture current settings).

[BDMerge Froxel F0] MASTER GATE for the hybrid froxel volumetrics grid (camera-frustum froxel atlas carrying the shared atmosphere). Default OFF = zero froxel code runs, zero targets allocate, output byte-identical. Independent of the per-cone BDMergeProjectorVolumetrics path, which is unchanged. F0 builds only the grid + media pass + debug visualizer - no lighting yet.
[BDMerge Froxel F0] Froxel grid width in cells across the frustum (16-512; default 240). Higher = finer horizontal detail at higher atlas cost. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.
[BDMerge Froxel F0] Froxel grid height in cells across the frustum (16-512; default 136). Higher = finer vertical detail at higher atlas cost. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Froxel grid depth in exponentially-distributed Z slices (clamped to 16-128; default 64). Packed into a 2D Z-slice atlas (tilesX = ceil(sqrt(GridZ)), tilesY = ceil(GridZ/tilesX)). Higher = smoother depth gradient at higher atlas cost. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Far distance of the froxel grid in metres (8.0-1024.0; default 128.0). The exponential Z slices span from the camera near plane to this distance. Beyond it there is no froxel medium. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Base extinction (sigma_t) of the froxel medium per metre (0.0-4.0; default 0.02). The uniform air density before height fog and noise modulate it. In the F0 debug view this is the mid-ramp value (red saturates at 2x this). Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Height-fog blend for the froxel medium (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = OFF). Blends the base density toward an altitude-dependent falloff (denser near ground, thinner up high). Raise it in the debug view to see a ground-hugging density gradient. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Height-fog density multiplier at/below the ground reference altitude (0.0-4.0; default 1.0). The medium is densest here and thins with altitude per BDMergeFroxelFogFalloff. Only active when BDMergeFroxelFogStrength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel F0/F4] Height-fog e-fold falloff distance in metres (0.5-256.0; default 3.0). Over this many metres of altitude above the ground reference the density falls to ~37% of the ground value. Small values (2-5) give a visible fog "surface" at set scale; the old default of 20 was imperceptible over a room-height span. Only active when BDMergeFroxelFogStrength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel F0/F4] Height reference for the froxel ground fog. In the default agent-relative mode (BDMergeFroxelFogBaseMode 1) this is an OFFSET in metres from your avatar's feet: 0 = fog layer top right at your feet, +2 = waist-height fog, negative sinks it below the floor. Anchored to the avatar (not the camera) so the layer stays put during flycam moves and works at any skybox altitude. In mode 0 it is a legacy absolute region-Z altitude. Density equals FogGroundDensity at and below the reference and thins above it per FogFalloff. Only active when BDMergeFroxelFogStrength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel F4] How BDMergeFroxelFogBase is interpreted: 1 (default) = relative offset from the avatar's feet (usable range roughly -10..+10; deterministic during flycam camera moves); 0 = legacy absolute region-Z altitude (0-4096, only useful if you need the layer pinned to a world height independent of where you stand).

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Animated 3D value-noise medium strength (0.0-1.0; default 0.0 = OFF). Modulates the froxel density with a slow, low-frequency world-anchored fbm so the air has drifting dust motes instead of being flat. Raise it in the debug view to see drifting mottling. TASTEFUL LEVER - a subtle value is ~0.2-0.35. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Spatial scale of the animated noise medium in cycles per metre (0.01-2.0; default 0.25). Lower = larger, softer clouds; higher = finer detail. Only active when BDMergeFroxelNoiseStrength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel F0/F5] Master scroll speed of the animated noise medium in metres per second (-2.0..2.0; default 0.1). Multiplies the BDMergeFroxelWindX/Y/Z direction vector to give the actual drift velocity; negative reverses the drift along the wind vector. Slow drift reads as gently settling dust. Only active when BDMergeFroxelNoiseStrength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel] Dust-wind compass bearing in degrees (0-360; default 0 = true north). This is the direction the wind comes FROM; by default the dust drifts the OPPOSITE way, so 0 = a north wind blowing toward the south. Toggle BDMergeFroxelWindInverted to blow toward the bearing instead. Steers both the froxel air and projector-beam dust; the drift SPEED is BDMerge*NoiseSpeed. Only active when noise strength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel] Dust-wind vertical tilt in degrees (-90..90; default 0 = level). Positive = wind comes from above so the dust drifts DOWNWARD (settling); negative rises. Combined with BDMergeFroxelWindInverted. Only active when noise strength > 0.

[BDMerge Froxel] Invert the dust-wind direction: OFF (default) = the dust blows the OPPOSITE way to the Azimuth bearing (meteorological: a north wind blows south); ON = it blows TOWARD the Azimuth bearing instead.

[BDMerge Froxel F1] Uniform ambient in-scatter radiance of the froxel medium - the "air glow" (0.0-8.0; default 0.35). At 0 the fog only extinguishes (darkens/occludes distant geometry); above 0 it also glows softly, reading as atmospheric haze. This is the medium's only light source until per-light injection (F2) adds real lights on top. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F2] When the froxel master (BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics) is on, inject volumetric-flagged projectors INTO the froxel grid (one flat integration cost for all of them) INSTEAD of rendering their per-cone shafts. Default ON. Turn it OFF for the F1 look (ambient-only fog) with the per-cone shafts untouched - the A/B lever between the old sharp-shaft path and the new soft-grid beams. Injected projectors are automatically excluded from the per-cone pass so they never double-light. No effect unless BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Froxel F2] Maximum number of projector light-injection passes per frame (clamped 1-16; default 8). Volumetric-flagged projectors are injected in shadow-slot order up to this cap; any beyond it are skipped this frame (logged to the Pipeline debug tag, not spammed). Each pass is a cheap ~2MP additive atlas draw. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics and BDMergeFroxelLights are on.

[BDMerge Froxel F3] Froxel-space temporal accumulation of the light atlas. Default ON (froxel is opt-in overall, and the jittered injection this enables NEEDS the resolve to average). When ON: the injection samples are jittered per frame and a resolve pass reprojects each froxel's world position into the previous frame's grid, neighborhood-clamps, and EMA-blends - beams in fog become smoother/less steppy over ~a second when the camera holds, with NO trailing/ghost when panning (the reprojection is pure world-space grid-to-grid, no surface depth, so a beam cannot ghost against a wall). When OFF: no jitter, no resolve, and the integrate pass reads the raw injected light atlas directly = exactly the F2 look (slightly steppier but identical layout). Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics and BDMergeFroxelLights are on.

[BDMerge Froxel F3] Froxel light-atlas history EMA weight (0.0-0.95; default 0.9; clamped in code). How much of the reprojected, neighborhood-clamped previous frame is blended into each froxel's light this frame: higher = smoother/more denoised beams but slower to converge on change; 0 disables accumulation (pure current frame, still jittered so it shimmers). The neighborhood clamp bounds it so it cannot smear. Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics, BDMergeFroxelLights and BDMergeFroxelTemporal are on.

[BDMerge Froxel F0] Froxel debug visualizer overlay. 0 = off, 1 = show media density at the surface froxel (fullscreen 50% overlay, black->green->yellow->red ramp over 0->2x BDMergeFroxelDensity - proves froxel coords line up with the scene), 2 = show one middle Z-slice tile stretched fullscreen (proves the atlas tiling), 3 = [F1] show the INTEGRATED atlas in-scatter radiance L at the surface froxel (validates the integrate pass independently of the scene composite), 4 = [F2] show the LIGHT atlas injected in-scatter source at the surface froxel (shows where each projector lit the grid; raise Density so the beams read). Only active when BDMergeFroxelVolumetrics is on.

[BDMerge Batch 2] Master gate for soft (contact-hardening + filled) shadows. Default OFF = classic hard 5-tap projector/sun shadows, byte-identical to before. When ON, the projector-shadow PCF kernel widens with receiver distance (a physically-motivated penumbra that is sharp at contact and softer farther away) and shadowed pixels are lifted off pure black toward an ambient fill floor. See BDMergeSoftShadowSoftness / MaxPenumbra / Fill / Sun for the sub-controls.

[BDMerge Batch 2] Soft-shadow penumbra rate (0.0-16.0; default 3.0). The per-light source-size term: how fast the PCF kernel widens with the receiver's distance from the light. Higher = softer, wider penumbrae. Only active when BDMergeSoftProjectorShadows is on.

[BDMerge Batch 2] Hard cap on the soft-shadow penumbra kernel radius in shadow-map texels (1.0-16.0; default 6.0). Bounds how blurry a distant shadow edge can get and keeps the widened PCF cost bounded. Only active when BDMergeSoftProjectorShadows is on.

[BDMerge Batch 2] Ambient shadow-fill floor (0.0-1.0; default 0.15). Lifts fully shadowed regions off pure black toward this value so projector shadows read like real shadows (ambient/bounce fill) instead of crushing to black. 0 = no fill. Only active when BDMergeSoftProjectorShadows is on.

[BDMerge Batch 2] Also apply the contact-hardening + fill model to the sun/moon cascade shadows (default OFF), for consistency with softened projector shadows. When off the sun path is byte-identical to before even if BDMergeSoftProjectorShadows is on.

[Vogel A/B] Soft-shadow kernel selector. Default OFF (0) = the fixed 12-tap Poisson-disk soft-shadow kernel, byte-identical to before (baseline for the A/B). ON (1) = Vogel-disk PCF with a per-pixel spatial rotation (interleaved gradient noise), which turns the fixed disk's banding in wide penumbrae into fine grain that reads as smoother. The rotation is spatial only (no per-frame animation) so it stays stable under the ReShade TAAU / motion-vector chain. Only active when BDMergeSoftProjectorShadows (and, for the sun cascades, BDMergeSoftShadowSun) is on. See RenderShadowSoftTaps for the tap count.

[Vogel A/B] Vogel-disk soft-shadow tap count (8-32; default 16). Number of shadow-map samples in the Vogel PCF kernel when RenderShadowSoftVogel is on. Higher = smoother penumbra grain at higher shadow-sampling cost; clamped to 32. Ignored when RenderShadowSoftVogel is off.

[BDMerge Batch 2] Gobo/cookie mip + anisotropic filtering (default ON). Sets a trilinear-mip + anisotropic filter state on the projector cookie texture and clamps the shader's focus-based cookie LOD up to the screen-space minification LOD, so a projected gobo viewed at a grazing angle or from far away stays crisp instead of aliasing. Only affects projector cookie sampling; turn off to restore the old fixed-LOD cookie look.
